title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Marine
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Coast Guard confirms malicious cyber activity on a US-bound tanker, while an LNG-carrier control-system claim stays unverified
items.content_text: The US Coast Guard and FBI boarded two US-bound tankers in late August, VL Prosperity on 21 August and the LPG carrier Kohaku on 24 August, after indications that their networks were compromised. Rear Adm. Amy Grable said investigators found malicious cyber activity on VL Prosperity’s IT and operational systems, yet the Coast Guard reports no operational disruption, vessel instability, danger to crews or environmental impact. Claims that attackers raised engine speed and cut communications for about 30 hours come from Iranian media and are unconfirmed. No attribution has been confirmed, though US officials are examining an Iran link. Separately, LNG carrier Vivit Africa LNG lost access to some control systems in early September; its crew alleges hackers took control, but Italy’s Coast Guard recorded only a cargo-monitoring malfunction of undetermined cause. Bloomberg reports nearly 20 ships are being tracked.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: TechCrunch, 18 Sep 2026 (Coast Guard/FBI statement); CBS News (Rear Adm. Grable); Digital Ship; Splash247 (crew claims); Bloomberg via gCaptain, 18 Sep; Dragos, 24 Sep
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Attack on VL Prosperity reported 7 Aug near Gibraltar; boardings 21 & 24 Aug; Vivit Africa LNG incident early Sep 2026; no official update found after 24 Sep

items.title: Port of Tanjung Pelepas restarted in phases after a cyber incident halted container operations
items.content_text: A cyber incident detected late on 9 September forced Malaysia’s Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP), a joint venture of MMC Group and APM Terminals, to suspend container-terminal operations as a precaution; the terminal operating systems were affected. A phased restart began on 10 September with manual processing for export container gate-ins, and a PTP statement reported by WorldCargo News on 15 September said container operations had resumed with system recovery “advancing steadily.” The Direwolf ransomware group listed the port on its leak site on 11 September, claiming about 200 GB of data (per ransomware.live); PTP has not confirmed ransomware or any group, so that remains a claim. No newer development was found as of 29 September.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: WorldCargo News, 15 Sep 2026, quoting PTP (primary statement); Direwolf listing via ransomware.live, 11 Sep (claim)
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Incident 9 Sep 2026; phased restart from 10 Sep; operations resumed per 15 Sep statement

items.title: Cisco Secure FMC, a common firewall console at IT/OT boundaries, remains under active exploitation
items.content_text: Cisco Talos tracks three clusters exploiting Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center flaws. UAT-12197 deployed web shells and harvested credentials via CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0, unauthenticated authentication bypass to root code execution). UAT-11823, tied by Talos to Sandworm through tooling overlap, deployed a Cyclops Blink implant. UAT-11988, a ransomware operator, deployed Qilin after reconnaissance and tunneling. CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3) is a related low-privilege login flaw. Talos names no victims, sectors or countries, and its post was last updated 21 September. Editorial assessment: FMC often manages the firewalls between corporate IT and terminal-operating-system, crane and gate networks at ports.
tags: Incident — Exploited firewall management platform, CISA KEV

_otthreatfeed.category: Incident — Exploited firewall management platform, CISA KEV

items.title: ENISA: China-nexus intrusion sets showed continuous interest in transport, including maritime entities
items.content_text: The EU cybersecurity agency’s Threat Landscape 2026 report, covering calendar 2025 and published 22–23 September, says China-nexus intrusion sets showed continuous interest in the transport sector, including maritime entities, per Industrial Cyber’s summary. Transport ranked fourth among the most-affected sectors at 8%. Ransomware remained the most damaging threat, and 60% of unauthorized-access incidents leveraged known vulnerabilities. The report describes long-running intelligence-collection interest rather than a specific new operation against ships or ports, and it does not name a vessel or terminal victim.

items.title: Anthropic: an Iran-linked actor used its AI model to track US Navy vessels and research maritime VSAT flaws
items.content_text: Anthropic reported on 11 September that an Iran-linked actor used its Claude model to build Python pipelines for collecting open-source information on US naval positions, and to compile “targeting handbooks” with personnel rosters drawn from military photos, transponder identifiers and satellite-imagery scripts. The actor also directed the model to compile vulnerability research on shipboard systems, including maritime VSAT terminals, Cisco communications equipment and industrial control products. Anthropic banned the account, built new detection and shared intelligence with government authorities. The targets were naval, not commercial shipping, and the report describes reconnaissance and research, not intrusion into any vessel. No newer development was found as of 29 September.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Anthropic threat report, 11 Sep 2026, as reported by gCaptain and Navy Times (11 Sep 2026)

items.title: Honeywell survey: 87% of maritime respondents reported a significant OT incident in the past year
items.content_text: Honeywell’s 2026 OT Cybersecurity Benchmark, published 22 September and based on more than 600 industrial security leaders worldwide, found that 87% of maritime respondents reported a significant OT cybersecurity incident in the past 12 months, and 40% of maritime respondents named outdated equipment as their main obstacle. Across all sectors only 21% kept a complete OT asset inventory and average downtime from major incidents was 16.2 hours. This is a vendor survey of self-reported incidents; definitions of “significant” vary and it identifies no specific vessel or port.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Honeywell press release, 22 Sep 2026 (primary); Industrial Cyber

items.title: Citrix NetScaler RCE zero-days (CVSS 9.5 each) exploited before patches; CISA adds both to KEV
items.content_text: Citrix disclosed two NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws on 27 September, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, both CVSS 9.5 (v4), after watchTowr warned publicly on 26 September; both were exploited in the wild before a fix existed. CVE-2026-88771 is an unauthenticated command-injection flaw affecting NetScaler deployments generally, with no workaround reported; CVE-2026-88772 needs DTLS enabled, the default on VPN virtual servers. CISA added both to KEV on 27 September with a 30 September federal deadline and said exploitation is global. Fixed builds include 14.1-73.37 and 13.1-64.23 plus FIPS/NDcPP equivalents. Editorial assessment: NetScaler Gateway is a common remote-access front door into port, terminal and OT DMZ networks.
tags: Advisory — Zero-days exploited before a fix, CISA KEV

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — Zero-days exploited before a fix, CISA KEV

items.title: Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard hard-coded keys: CISA advisory names two CVEs and the fixed build
items.content_text: CISA’s advisory ICSA-26-258-02 (15 September) covers two hard-coded cryptographic key flaws (CWE-321) in Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard 5.07.0923.01, a shipboard fleet-optimization system: CVE-2026-81855 in its robot testing framework and CVE-2026-78225 in its deployer Update Controller. Per CISA, an attacker could deliver an unauthorized update, execute code or extract credentials. The CVE record lists 5.08.4052.01 as the fixed version. Published severity scores differ between sources, so check the advisory for the current rating. Wärtsilä says the flaws are not exploitable when the product is installed as recommended, and Cydome, which reported them, credits the vendor with a patch. No exploitation has been reported. A hard-coded key is shared across installations, so one recovered key could work fleet-wide.
tags: Advisory — Hard-coded cryptographic keys, fix available, no known exploitation

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — Hard-coded cryptographic keys, fix available, no known exploitation

items.title: CISA and the FBI name transportation among sectors exposed through a compromised ICS integrator
items.content_text: A joint FBI/CISA fact sheet on working with third-party ICS integrators, published 24 September, describes foreign cyber actors who compromised a US industrial automation company in March–April 2025 and created nine .zip files of about 800 files, including SCADA-related data, for presumed exfiltration. It names power utilities and transportation among the affected customers. It urges least privilege for integrators, secured remote-access points, offline backups and cybersecurity terms in contracts. Editorial assessment: shipyards, OEMs and other service providers often hold standing remote access to vessel and terminal control systems, so the guidance applies directly to marine operators.
tags: Guidance — Third-party ICS integrator remote access

_otthreatfeed.category: Guidance — Third-party ICS integrator remote access

items.title: Coast Guard announces a dedicated Office of Maritime Cybersecurity Policy
items.content_text: The US Coast Guard announced on 31 August that it has established an Office of Maritime Cybersecurity Policy (CG-MCP) under the Director of Inspections and Compliance (CG-5PC). It is meant to be the Coast Guard’s central authority for cyber policy for the Marine Transportation System, directing a coordinated compliance and enforcement strategy and acting as the main liaison to industry. It arrives as the MTSA cybersecurity rule phases in: incident reporting has applied since July 2025, and a Cybersecurity Officer, assessment and approved plan are due by 16 July 2027 (per Dragos’ 24 September summary of the rule).
